designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: Clean, legible icon grid and a relatable deadpan line, and it reads well as a white-on-black chest block. But the punchline is jammed right under the last row of labels with no breathing room while the bottom quarter of the print is empty, so the payoff looks like a fifth row of labels rather than the punchline. A few icons are weak or off-model (the airbag figure, DOOR OPEN, the TRACTION CONTROL squiggles), and HIGH BEAM isn't a warning at all, which undercuts the 'everything is lit' gag. The 'this is fine' joke is a familiar one, so it sells on execution, and the execution isn't quite there.
designs.fix: Give PROBABLY FINE clear space above it (about one row's height), make it larger to fill the empty bottom, and swap HIGH BEAM and the weak icons for real warning lights drawn accurately.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: The strongest of the three. The repeated 'Turn around.' is a joke every dog owner gets, the brush drawings are warm and loose, the poses go from standing to curled up, and the 'Sigh.' ending lands. It looks like a gift and reads well at a glance. Weak points: the step 3 dog's anatomy is muddled (the floating arc and the twisted head read as an error, not as motion), and the thin serif title and small italic captions will fill in or fade when printed small, especially on black.
designs.fix: Redraw step 3 so the turning pose is unmistakable, and thicken the title and caption type a little so they hold up on a printed tee.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: The cat-prefers-the-box joke is universally understood and the line art is crisp and printable. But panel 3 is confusing: the box breaks out of the frame and its lower sides merge into the panel border, so the box and the frame read as one shape, and a stray horizontal line runs behind the bed. The caption is small and its wording ('not sold separately') makes you stop and work it out instead of laughing. It's also a well-worn gag, so the drawing has to be flawless, and it isn't.
designs.fix: Rebuild panel 3 so the box sits cleanly inside (or deliberately and clearly over) the frame with no merged lines, and make the caption bigger and snappier.
